job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: In the small village of Rampur, young Arjun and his grandmother, Meena, sat on the porch watching the monsoon rain. Arjun asked why the soil in their backyard was so sticky and dark compared to the sandy soil near the riverbank. Meena explained that the dark soil, known as Regur, is formed by the weathering of volcanic rocks over millions of years. She pointed to a calendar on the wall dated 1994, which marked the year they moved to this farm. Meena noted that the high clay content in the Regur soil allows it to hold moisture exceptionally well, which is why farmers prefer it for growing cotton. Arjun wondered if all dark soils were equally fertile. Meena laughed and shook her head, explaining that fertility depends on mineral composition, not just color. She mentioned that in 2012, a soil testing team visited the neighboring village of Kolar to study these variations. Arjun realized that understanding the earth beneath his feet was more complex than he had imagined. He decided to help Meena plant seeds in the moist, dark patches, hoping for a bountiful harvest by the end of the season.
response.summary: Arjun and his grandmother discuss the characteristics of different soil types in their village. They explore how volcanic activity creates fertile soil and why moisture retention is crucial for farming. The story highlights the importance of understanding soil composition for agricultural success.
